letter:0.en: The rain hammered the window. On my desk lay a single envelope, no stamp, no return address. Inside, one *letter* — not a word, just the symbol G, cut from a printed page. Grey Crow had warned me: in Harbor City, one character could carry a death sentence.
letter:0.cnHint: 我的桌上出现了一封神秘信件，里面只有一个____，让我背脊发凉。
letter:0.line: 'One *letter* can open a door — or seal a grave,' Grey Crow said.

sheet:0.en: Ali spread a *sheet* of transparent plastic across the table. Beneath it, a hand-drawn map of the old port district glowed faint blue under my lamp. Every exit was marked with a small red cross. Someone had already planned our route — before we even took the case.
sheet:0.cnHint: 阿栗铺开一____地图，上面每个出口都被人提前标好了记号。
sheet:0.hook: None of the crosses pointed home.

corresponding:0.en: I pulled up the signal log on my screen. Each encrypted burst had a *corresponding* timestamp, and every timestamp matched a blackout in the city grid. This was no coincidence. Someone was sending messages the moment the cameras went blind. Zero. It had to be Zero.
corresponding:0.cnHint: 每一条加密信号都有____的停电记录，这绝非巧合。
corresponding:0.hook: The next blackout was in four minutes.

choose:0.en: Grey Crow placed two data chips on the table. 'One holds the safe route out. The other holds the truth about Zero.' He stepped back into the shadow. 'You can only *choose* one. The other burns.' My hand hovered over both. The rain outside grew louder.
choose:0.cnHint: 引路人给我两个芯片，让我____其中一个，另一个将被销毁。
choose:0.hook: My fingers stopped over the wrong one.
choose:0.line: '*Choose* fast — Zero is already moving,' Grey Crow said quietly.

single:0.en: I reviewed the night's intercepts. Forty-three encrypted messages, all traced to different nodes across Harbor City — yet every one carried a *single* repeating pattern buried in the noise. Ali spotted it first. Three dots, a pause, two dots. Over and over. Someone was calling for help.
single:0.cnHint: 四十三条加密消息中隐藏着同一个____重复信号，有人在求救。
single:0.hook: The pattern stopped the moment I found it.
single:0.line: 'There is only one *single* voice in all this noise,' Ali said.

line:0.en: Ali traced her finger along the wall map. 'Follow this *line*,' she said, drawing a path from the old market to the coastal relay tower. 'Every coded broadcast tonight passed through this exact corridor.' I stared at the thin mark on the paper. It cut straight through Zero's territory.
line:0.cnHint: 阿栗在地图上画出一条____，所有加密广播都经过这条走廊。
line:0.line: 'Stay on this *line* and do not stop for anything,' Ali said.

become:0.en: I opened the oldest case file in the city archive. The rookie investigator in the first photo looked clean, hopeful. I barely recognised him. In Harbor City, the rain gets into everything. You do not notice the moment you *become* someone harder, someone colder. I closed the file fast.
become:0.cnHint: 翻看旧档案，我突然意识到自己已____了另一个人。
become:0.hook: The face in the photo did not smile back.
become:0.line: 'Do not let this city *become* your whole world,' Grey Crow said.

centre:0.en: The signal traced back to an abandoned data hub in the *centre* of the Kowlong district. Ali confirmed it: all encrypted traffic in Harbor City passed through that single building at least once. Whoever held that hub held every secret in the city. Grey Crow had known all along.
centre:0.cnHint: 所有加密信号都经过九龙区____的一栋废弃大楼，那里藏着城市的全部秘密。
centre:0.hook: Grey Crow's name was in the oldest log.
centre:0.line: 'The *centre* of this web is closer than you think,' Grey Crow said.

bank:0.en: The rain hit the window like static. I opened my terminal and pulled up the suspect's *bank* records — row after row of small transfers, all made at 3 a.m. Ali leaned over my shoulder. 'That pattern,' she said. 'Someone is draining it slowly, so no alarm trips.' The screen flickered.
bank:0.cnHint: 我调出嫌疑人的____记录，发现深夜有规律的小额转账。
bank:0.hook: The last transfer was made sixty seconds ago.
bank:0.line: 'Check the *bank* records — every entry after midnight.'

statement:0.en: Grey Crow slid a folded paper across the wet table. 'Read it,' he said. It was a *statement* from a dock worker — three lines, careful handwriting — claiming he saw Zero near the signal tower the night the broadcast went dark. I read it twice. The words were too clean, too neat.
statement:0.cnHint: 引路人递来一份目击者的____，但内容干净得令人生疑。
statement:0.hook: Clean words mean someone rewrote the truth.
statement:0.line: 'That *statement* was written by someone other than the dock worker.'

identify:0.en: The room smelled of damp wire and cold coffee. A grid of faces filled my screen — fifty contacts pulled from Zero's encrypted channel. My job was simple: *identify* the one who leaked the city frequency map. Ali set a timer. 'Twenty minutes before they know we are looking,' she said quietly.
identify:0.cnHint: 我必须从零点的联络人名单中____出泄露地图的人。
identify:0.hook: One face in the grid was already watching me back.
identify:0.line: 'I can *identify* the leak — give me the channel log.'

comprehension:0.en: Grey Crow handed me a decoded file. The words were plain English, but their meaning stayed dark. My *comprehension* of the cipher system was still thin — I had studied it for only two nights. Ali watched me struggle. 'The city built this language to be forgotten,' she said. 'That is the point.'
comprehension:0.cnHint: 我对密码系统的____还很薄弱，面对解码文件仍感到茫然。
comprehension:0.hook: The file had a countdown buried in its last line.
comprehension:0.line: 'Your *comprehension* of this cipher will decide if we survive tonight.'

require:0.en: The system prompt blinked red. A new case had arrived — priority level four. I read the briefing twice. It would *require* access to the sealed frequency archive, a place only Grey Crow had keys to. Outside, rain hammered the glass. I typed his name into the contact field and waited.
require:0.cnHint: 新案件____进入封存的频率档案库，而钥匙只有引路人有。
require:0.hook: Grey Crow's status light showed he was already online.
require:0.line: 'This mission will *require* more than a rookie investigator.'

least:0.en: Zero had left three possible routes through the server maze. I mapped all three on the desk screen. The longest path was the safest. The shortest was a trap — I could see that at once. The middle route was the *least* obvious, which, in Zero's logic, made it the most dangerous of all.
least:0.cnHint: 三条路线中，最不起眼的那条____明显，反而最危险。
least:0.hook: Zero always hides the real trap in plain sight.
least:0.line: 'Choose the path that draws the *least* attention — then double-check it.'

following:0.en: I found the note taped under the desk lamp. It was short: a time, a floor number, one word — 'come.' The *following* morning, Ali was gone. Her coat still hung on the chair. Her coffee was still warm. I picked up the note and read the time again. It was now.
following:0.cnHint: ____天早上，阿栗不见了，只留下一张便条和一杯热咖啡。
following:0.hook: The floor number on the note did not exist in this building.
following:0.line: 'The *following* hours are the most dangerous — stay close to me.'

decide:0.en: Two signals were coming in at once — one from Grey Crow, one from an unknown source. My console could handle only one. I had ten seconds to *decide*. Ali's voice crackled through the room speaker: 'Whatever you pick, commit to it. Hesitation is the only thing that will get us caught.'
decide:0.cnHint: 两个信号同时涌入，我必须在十秒内____接收哪一个。
decide:0.hook: The unknown signal began transmitting my own name.
decide:0.line: '*Decide* now — we do not get a second chance at this.'

passage:0.en: The rain hammered the roof of the old archive room. Grey Crow slid a folded paper across the table. 'Read this *passage* carefully,' he said. The words were plain, but between the lines I could feel a signal — something cold, something urgent, meant only for me.
passage:0.cnHint: 灰鸦让我仔细阅读一段文字，其中似乎藏着只有我能感知的____。
passage:0.hook: The last word on the page was my own name.
passage:0.line: 'This *passage* holds the only map you will ever need.'

base:0.en: Ali set her toolkit on the *base* of the tall server rack and knelt down. The floor was wet. Somewhere in the tangle of cables below, a small device blinked — one pulse every three seconds. She looked up at me and said nothing. That silence was its own kind of answer.
base:0.cnHint: 阿栗在机柜____部发现了一个每三秒闪烁一次的神秘装置。
base:0.hook: One more blink, and the whole grid would go dark.
base:0.line: 'Check the *base* — something down there does not belong.'

section:0.en: I pulled up the city map on the cracked monitor. Grey Crow tapped a finger on the harbour district. 'This *section* has been dark for six hours,' he said. No signals, no traffic, no faces on record. In Harbor City, silence like that was never an accident — it was a warning.
section:0.cnHint: 灰鸦指出地图上某个____已经沉默了整整六小时。
section:0.hook: Zero's last known location was right at the centre.
section:0.line: 'Every *section* of this city talks — except that one.'

answer:0.en: The terminal screen flickered twice and then stopped. I had typed the same query four times. No *answer* came back. Ali leaned over my shoulder and whispered that the system was listening but refusing to speak. In Harbor City, a machine that chooses silence is far more dangerous than one that lies.
answer:0.cnHint: 终端对我的查询毫无____，阿栗说沉默的机器比说谎的更危险。
answer:0.hook: Then a single character appeared — a question mark.
answer:0.line: 'The *answer* is in there — it just does not want to come out.'

study:0.en: Grey Crow's *study* was a narrow room packed with old paper files and dim yellow light. He never used the city net — too easy to trace. I sat across from him and watched him open a folder thick with coded notes. Outside, rain filled every crack in the street.
study:0.cnHint: 灰鸦的____里堆满了纸质档案，他从不联网以防被追踪。
study:0.hook: The top file had my case number on it — dated two years ago.
study:0.line: 'Welcome to my *study* — no signal reaches this room.'

mark:0.en: Ali pointed to the inside of the door frame. There, scratched into the old paint, was a small *mark* — a circle with one broken edge. 'Zero leaves these,' she said quietly. It meant someone in this building had been chosen as a target. I checked the room number. It was mine.
mark:0.cnHint: 阿栗在门框上发现了零点留下的____，那意味着有人已成为目标。
mark:0.hook: The paint around the mark was still fresh.
mark:0.line: 'That *mark* means Zero has already been here tonight.'

choice:0.en: Grey Crow closed the folder and looked at me across the table. 'You have one *choice*,' he said. 'Take the case and stay in the dark with us, or walk out and forget this room ever existed.' The rain outside grew louder. I had come this far. I already knew I was not walking out.
choice:0.cnHint: 灰鸦给了我唯一的____：接下这个案子，或者永远遗忘这个房间。
choice:0.hook: My hand was already reaching for the folder.
choice:0.line: 'Think carefully — this *choice* cannot be taken back.'

part:0.en: Ali spread the device on the table in three neat rows of small components. 'This *part* here,' she said, touching a tiny black chip, 'does not match the rest of the unit. It was added later, by someone who knew exactly what they were doing.' The chip was no bigger than a raindrop.
part:0.cnHint: 阿栗拆解装置后发现某个____与其他组件不符，是后来被人刻意加入的。
part:0.hook: The chip's code signature matched Zero's known signature exactly.
part:0.line: 'This *part* was never in the original design — someone planted it.'

passage:1.en: Rain hammered the old district. Grey Crow led me through a narrow *passage* between two crumbling walls, where coded graffiti covered every brick. 'Read the symbols,' he said. 'They point to Zero.' The tunnel smelled of rust and secrets. Somewhere ahead, a door clicked shut.
passage:1.cnHint: 灰鸦带我穿过一条隐秘的____，墙上满是暗语涂鸦。
passage:1.hook: The door had locked itself from the inside.
passage:1.line: 'This *passage* is the only way Zero ever moves through the old district.'

base:1.en: Ali pulled me to the edge of a fire tower and pointed down. At the *base* of the structure, someone had carved a string of numbers into the concrete. 'That code changes every midnight,' Ali whispered. Grey Crow was already crouching there, copying the digits into a wet notebook.
base:1.cnHint: 阿栗发现高塔____处刻着一串神秘数字。
base:1.hook: The last digit had been scratched out — tonight.
base:1.line: 'Check the *base* of every tower in this section; Zero always leaves a mark there.'

section:1.en: The city map on my lens showed Harbor City split into grids. One *section* in the east glowed red — a dead zone where signals vanished. Grey Crow tapped that block twice. 'Zero operates from there,' he said. Ali looked uneasy. Nobody we knew had come back from that grid.
section:1.cnHint: 地图上某个____区域信号消失，据说是零点的地盘。
section:1.hook: My lens flickered, then went completely dark.
section:1.line: 'That *section* of the city swallows every signal we send in.'

answer:1.en: I knocked three times on the iron shutter, the way Grey Crow had told me. Silence. Then, slowly, a slot opened at eye level and a pair of cold eyes stared out. An *answer* finally came — not words, but a folded card pushed through the gap. On it: a single street corner drawn in red ink.
answer:1.cnHint: 铁闸后终于传来一个____，不是话语，而是一张纸条。
answer:1.hook: The corner on the card was two blocks behind me.
answer:1.line: 'That card is your *answer* — get to that corner before the rain stops.'

study:1.en: Grey Crow spread six intercepted broadcasts on the hood of a parked truck. 'One hour,' he said. 'That is all the time you have to *study* these before they self-erase.' I leaned in, rain dripping off my hood onto the paper. Ali stood watch, eyes scanning every passing shadow.
study:1.cnHint: 灰鸦要我在一小时内____六份会自动销毁的情报。
study:1.hook: At fifty-nine minutes, the first sheet began to smoke.
study:1.line: '*Study* the third broadcast first — it hides the meeting point.'

mark:1.en: Someone had left a chalk *mark* on the lamppost outside the noodle stall — a small triangle pointing left. Grey Crow had taught me what triangles meant: a tail. I was being followed. I kept walking, kept my pace even, and did not look back. Ali was already circling around.
mark:1.cnHint: 路灯柱上的粉笔____暗示我正被人跟踪。
mark:1.line: 'That *mark* means someone in this street already knows your face.'

choice:1.en: Zero's voice came through a cracked speaker bolted to a wall: 'You have one *choice* — leave the data chip on the bench and walk away, or I broadcast your real name to every enforcer in the city.' Rain filled the silence. I looked at the bench. I looked at the dark street ahead.
choice:1.cnHint: 零点通过广播逼我做出一个____：留下芯片，或暴露身份。
choice:1.hook: My hand moved toward my pocket before my mind decided.
choice:1.line: 'Understand this: your only *choice* tonight is the one I am offering you.'

part:1.en: Grey Crow stopped me under a broken streetlight. 'The signal you heard is only one *part* of the message,' he said quietly. 'Zero splits every broadcast into three pieces and hides them across the city.' Two pieces were still out there, dissolving in the rain. I had maybe twenty minutes.
part:1.cnHint: 灰鸦提醒我，截获的信号只是完整情报的一个____。
part:1.hook: The second piece was broadcasting from my own coat pocket.
part:1.line: 'Find the missing *part* before midnight, or the whole message dies.'

blank:0.en: The encrypted file arrived at midnight. Every field was filled except one: a single *blank* near the bottom, shaped like a missing tooth. Grey Crow leaned over my shoulder and whispered that the missing entry was the most important one. Someone had erased it on purpose.
blank:0.cnHint: 加密文件底部有一处____，灰鸦说那里藏着关键信息。
blank:0.hook: Whatever was erased, Zero did not want us to find it.
blank:0.line: 'That *blank* is not empty — it is a trap.'

reading:0.en: Ali slid a data chip across the wet table. 'Your *reading* for tonight,' she said quietly. The chip held forty intercepted signals, each one a coded threat. I plugged it in and the room filled with cold blue light. Outside, rain hammered the window like a warning.
reading:0.cnHint: 阿栗交给我今晚的____任务，芯片里藏着四十条截获的威胁信号。
reading:0.hook: Signal thirty-nine carried a name — mine.
reading:0.line: 'Finish the *reading* before the clock hits two.'

list:0.en: A *list* appeared on my screen without warning — twelve names, no titles, no dates. Grey Crow recognized three of them as people who had vanished last winter. Ali locked the door without being asked. The air in the small office suddenly felt very thin.
list:0.cnHint: 屏幕上突然出现一份____，灰鸦认出了三个失踪者的名字。
list:0.hook: My own code-name sat at the very bottom.

item:0.en: Grey Crow pulled up the evidence log and pointed to the seventh *item*: a signal broadcast from inside the city's own police tower. No one was supposed to transmit from there after dark. Ali checked twice and the result did not change. We stared at each other in silence.
item:0.cnHint: 证据记录里第七条____显示，信号竟从警察塔内部发出。
item:0.hook: Whoever sent it was still inside the building.
item:0.line: 'That *item* alone can bring the whole tower down.'

select:0.en: The terminal asked me to *select* one channel from a hidden menu that should not have existed on a city-issue device. Each channel had a symbol instead of a name. Grey Crow said nothing; he only pointed at the one shaped like a broken eye. I clicked it.
select:0.cnHint: 终端出现一个隐藏菜单，要求我____一个频道，灰鸦指向了那个破碎眼睛的符号。
select:0.hook: The screen went dark, then began to speak.
select:0.line: '*Select* carefully — some doors cannot be closed again.'

need:0.en: The power in the block cut out at exactly 01:00. Ali lit a single small lamp. 'We *need* the backup drive before the grid comes back,' she said, already moving toward the shelf. Grey Crow blocked the door. Somewhere below us, boots were climbing the stairs fast.
need:0.cnHint: 停电后阿栗说我们____备份驱动器，但楼梯里已经传来了脚步声。
need:0.hook: The steps stopped — right outside our door.
need:0.line: 'We *need* that drive in the next thirty seconds.'

letter:1.en: Rain hammered the street. A sealed envelope lay wedged under a broken lamp post, addressed to no one. I tore it open. Inside, a single *letter* — not a word, just the character Z — was stamped in red ink. Grey Crow had warned me: in Harbor City, one symbol could mean a death order.
letter:1.cnHint: 我在路灯下发现一个信封，里面只有一个红色的____。
letter:1.hook: Z was Zero's mark, and Zero never warned twice.
letter:1.line: 'One *letter* is enough to end you,' Grey Crow said.

sheet:1.en: The rain had soaked everything. Pinned to a chain-link fence was a single *sheet* of paper, its ink bleeding but still readable. Twelve names. Mine was last. Ali grabbed my arm before I could move — someone had left this here on purpose, a trap dressed as a clue.
sheet:1.cnHint: 围栏上贴着一张____，上面写着十二个名字，我的排在最后。
sheet:1.hook: The ink was fresh — whoever posted it was still close.
sheet:1.line: 'This *sheet* was meant for your eyes only,' Ali whispered.

corresponding:1.en: Grey Crow slid me a coded map of Harbor City's lower grid. Each blinking node had a *corresponding* symbol on the back of my wrist — tattoos I never remembered getting. The rain washed the street clean but not my confusion. Someone had marked me long before I took this case.
corresponding:1.cnHint: 地图上每个节点都有一个与我手腕纹身____的符号。
corresponding:1.hook: I had been chosen for this job before I chose it.
corresponding:1.line: 'Find the *corresponding* signal and the door will open,' said Grey Crow.

choose:1.en: Two alleys split before me in the neon dark. Ali said left led to Zero's relay tower; right led to the safe house. The rain erased footprints fast. I had ten seconds to *choose*, and Grey Crow's voice crackled once in my earpiece: 'Wrong turn ends the mission.'
choose:1.cnHint: 两条小巷摆在我面前，我必须立刻____走哪一条。
choose:1.hook: My foot lifted — and the earpiece went dead.
choose:1.line: '*Choose* wrong tonight and there is no morning,' Ali said.

single:1.en: The broadcast tower above the market sent a *single* pulse every ninety seconds — a heartbeat for Harbor City's black-market network. I timed it, counted it, felt it hum through the wet iron railing. Zero used that pulse to move data. Tonight I planned to use it to move myself.
single:1.cnHint: 信号塔每九十秒发出____脉冲，我打算借此行动。
single:1.hook: The next pulse was in four seconds — ready or not.
single:1.line: 'A *single* mistake here and the whole grid goes dark,' Grey Crow said.

line:1.en: A glowing *line* of coded graffiti stretched the full length of the underpass wall, each symbol pulsing faintly in the rain. Grey Crow said it was a live message feed, updated by runners every hour. I pressed my palm to the cold concrete and felt the data moving beneath the paint like a second city.
line:1.cnHint: 地下通道的墙上有一条发光的涂鸦____，每小时更新一次。
line:1.hook: The last symbol had just changed — someone was watching me read it.
line:1.line: 'Follow that *line* to the end and you will find Zero,' Ali said.

become:1.en: I had been a signal analyst for two years. In one rainy night I had *become* something else — a target, a carrier, a piece on someone's board. The neon signs blurred in the downpour as I ran. Grey Crow's words rang in my head: Harbor City changes people, and not always slowly.
become:1.cnHint: 在这个雨夜，我悄然____了某人棋盘上的一颗棋子。
become:1.hook: The city had changed me — and I had not noticed until now.
become:1.line: 'You have *become* exactly what Zero wanted,' Grey Crow said coldly.

centre:1.en: The old transit hub stood at the *centre* of the lower grid, dark for twenty years but lit tonight by a pale blue glow from the top floor. Ali pointed without speaking. Every coded broadcast we had traced led here, to this dead building in the heart of a living city. Something was awake inside.
centre:1.cnHint: 废弃的交通枢纽位于下城区的____，今晚它亮灯了。
centre:1.hook: A shadow moved behind the top-floor glass — one figure, waiting.
centre:1.line: 'The *centre* of the grid is where Zero has always been,' Ali said.

blank:1.en: Rain hammered the street. A crumpled flyer lay under the lamppost, its printed text half-washed away. One line remained: a grid of boxes with every name crossed out except a single *blank* at the bottom. Someone had left space for one more person. My name, maybe.
blank:1.cnHint: 我在雨中发现一张传单，上面只剩一个____，似乎是留给我的。
blank:1.hook: Whose hand had left that space — and why?
blank:1.line: Grey Crow said, 'That *blank* was meant for you all along.'

reading:1.en: The alley wall was covered in coded graffiti. Ali knelt close, eyes moving fast. '*Reading* this takes a certain kind of mind,' she said quietly. Each symbol was a letter, each letter a warning. By the time I understood the last line, the wall had begun to glow.
reading:1.cnHint: 阿栗在小巷里仔细____墙上的密码涂鸦，发现了一个警告。
reading:1.hook: The glow meant someone knew we were here.
reading:1.line: Ali whispered, '*Reading* this wall just changed everything for us.'

list:1.en: Grey Crow slid a folded paper across the wet bench. I opened it under the streetlight. A *list* of twelve names, each one a signal carrier in Harbor City. Eleven were crossed out in red. The last name made my chest tighten. I knew that person.
list:1.cnHint: 灰鸦给了我一份____，上面十一个名字已被划掉，最后一个让我心跳加速。
list:1.hook: The last name on that list was someone I trusted.
list:1.line: Grey Crow said, 'Guard this *list* with your life — literally.'

item:1.en: The market stall was loud and bright despite the rain. Ali pointed to a small metal box on the third shelf. 'That *item*,' she said, keeping her voice flat. It looked like junk. But the serial number on its base matched the code Zero had broadcast last night.
item:1.cnHint: 阿栗在市场摊位上指出一个____，它的编号与零点昨晚的广播暗号吻合。
item:1.hook: Zero's code led here — but was it a trap?
item:1.line: Ali said, 'Buy that *item* and do not look at the seller.'

select:1.en: The terminal on the corner flickered in the rain. Three routes home glowed on the cracked screen. I had to *select* one fast — each path had a watcher, and staying still was worse. Grey Crow's voice crackled in my earpiece: wrong choice, and Zero wins tonight.
select:1.cnHint: 我必须在路口终端上____一条回家的路线，每条路都有人监视。
select:1.hook: My finger hovered — one route was already compromised.
select:1.line: Grey Crow urged, '*Select* the middle path and run, do not stop.'

need:1.en: The rain came harder. My coat was soaked through. I found the drop point — a rusted pipe near the bridge — but the package was gone. Zero had moved it. I *need* to think fast before the next signal window closes in four minutes, Ali had warned me.
need:1.cnHint: 我发现接货点的包裹已经消失，阿栗提醒我____尽快想出对策。
need:1.hook: Four minutes — and Zero was already watching the bridge.
need:1.line: Ali said, 'You *need* to move now; the window is closing fast.'

blank:2.en: The data chip cracked open on my desk. Inside, a single page — columns of intercepted code, all filled except one. That *blank* sat at the bottom like a held breath, waiting for a name or a signal I did not yet have. Outside, the rain hammered Harbor City without mercy.
blank:2.cnHint: 数据芯片里的文件上有一处____，调查员不知道该填什么。
blank:2.hook: Whatever filled that space would either save me or bury me.
blank:2.line: 'The *blank* at the bottom — that is what Zero wants us to find.'

reading:2.en: Grey Crow slid a thin card under my door before dawn. On it, a single line of encoded text — my first *reading* since joining the unit. The symbols shifted as I stared, the way harbor fog shifts over water: slow, deliberate, hiding something solid beneath.
reading:2.cnHint: 调查员收到灰鸦送来的一段____，试图破解其中的含义。
reading:2.hook: The final symbol was not code — it was a street address.
reading:2.line: 'Your *reading* for tonight — memorise it, then burn the card.'

list:2.en: Ali found it taped behind a broken vent in the east corridor: a folded sheet covered in usernames and frequencies. 'A *list*,' she said quietly, scanning each line with a small torch. Seventeen names. Ours were not on it. That should have felt safe. It did not.
list:2.cnHint: 阿里在通风口后发现了一张____，上面写满了用户名。
list:2.hook: Name eighteen had been torn away — deliberately, carefully, recently.
list:2.line: 'This *list* tells us who Zero trusts — and who he has already removed.'

item:2.en: The evidence shelf held dozens of seized objects. I reached for the last *item* on the right: a scratched metal tag no bigger than a coin. Grey Crow had flagged it three weeks ago, then gone silent. Under the desk lamp its surface showed faint pressed letters — a frequency.
item:2.cnHint: 调查员在证物架上找到了最后一件____，上面刻着一个频率。
item:2.hook: That frequency matched the signal we had been told did not exist.
item:2.line: 'Every *item* on that shelf is a clue — but this one is a warning.'

select:2.en: Zero's terminal was still warm when we reached it. The screen showed a menu of broadcast channels — most greyed out, one still glowing. Whoever had been here managed to *select* a single restricted frequency before vanishing. The cursor blinked in the empty room like a slow, patient heartbeat.
select:2.cnHint: 零点离开前在终端上____了一个受限频道，调查员发现了线索。
select:2.hook: That channel had been officially shut down four years ago.
select:2.line: 'They had seconds — yet they knew exactly which channel to *select*.'

need:2.en: The signal burst lasted three seconds. Ali replayed it twice, then looked up. 'We *need* the cipher key Grey Crow gave you — the one you memorised on the bridge.' I pulled the sequence from memory, digit by digit. The room felt smaller with each number. Rain ticked the glass.
need:2.cnHint: 阿里告诉调查员，破译信号____灰鸦之前给的密钥。
need:2.hook: The decoded message contained only four words: 'Do not trust Ali.'

bank:1.en: The rain hit the street like static noise. Grey Crow led me to the edge of the canal, where the dark *bank* dropped straight into black water. 'The data packet is hidden here,' he said, pressing a chip into my hand. Below, the city's glow bled into the current.
bank:1.cnHint: 灰鸦带我到运河____边，将一枚芯片塞进我手里。
bank:1.hook: Something moved in the water beneath us.
bank:1.line: 'The *bank* holds more than water tonight,' Grey Crow said.

statement:1.en: Zero's voice cut through the rain on every public speaker in the block. It was not music. It was a *statement* — seven words, looped, growing louder. Ali grabbed my sleeve. 'Those words are illegal in Harbor City,' she said. The neon signs above us flickered and went dark, one by one.
statement:1.cnHint: 零点通过街头广播发出一份____，阿栗告诉我那些话在城里是被禁止的。
statement:1.hook: The last sign died, and the street fell completely silent.
statement:1.line: 'That *statement* just broke three city codes,' Ali whispered.

identify:1.en: Coded graffiti covered the bridge wall — fifty symbols, all different. Grey Crow told me my job was to *identify* the one mark that did not belong. The rain was washing the paint away fast. I moved my flashlight slowly across the wall, searching, while footsteps echoed somewhere behind me.
identify:1.cnHint: 我必须在桥墙上的符号中____出那个异常标记，但雨水正在冲刷它们。
identify:1.line: 'Can you *identify* it before the rain takes it?' Grey Crow asked.

comprehension:1.en: The encrypted broadcast lasted four seconds. Ali played it back three times, her face tight. 'My *comprehension* of their code is about sixty percent,' she admitted, pulling her coat closer against the rain. That sixty percent was still enough to scare her. She turned the device off and looked at me with wide, careful eyes.
comprehension:1.cnHint: 阿栗对那段加密广播的____只有六成，但这已经足以让她感到恐慌。
comprehension:1.hook: 'The other forty percent,' she said, 'might be the worst part.'
comprehension:1.line: 'My *comprehension* of their signal stops right here,' Ali said.

require:1.en: The gate to the lower district was sealed. A small screen on the post read: entry will *require* a vocal pass-code, updated every hour. I had no pass-code. The rain hammered the pavement. Across the gate, a single light blinked in a window — the signal Grey Crow had told me to follow.
require:1.cnHint: 进入下城区的大门要求____声纹密码，而我根本没有。
require:1.hook: The light in the window blinked once more, then vanished.
require:1.line: 'They *require* a code I do not have,' I told Ali.

least:1.en: Three routes led away from the market. The longest was safe. The shortest was watched. The middle path was, at *least*, dark enough to hide in. I chose it without much hope. Ali moved ahead of me, silent as smoke, while the rain turned the narrow lane into a shallow river at our feet.
least:1.cnHint: 三条路各有风险，中间那条____还算能藏身，我们选择了它。
least:1.hook: A shadow at the far end of the lane stepped forward.
least:1.line: 'At *least* the dark is on our side,' Ali said quietly.

following:1.en: Zero left no name, no face — only instructions. The *following* message was scratched onto the back of a street sign in tiny, sharp letters: meet the source before dawn, or the data dies with it. I read it twice in the rain, then looked up. Every corner felt watched.
following:1.cnHint: 零点在路牌背面刻下____一段指令，要求我在黎明前找到那个消息源。
following:1.hook: Below the message, a second line had been added in fresh ink.
following:1.line: 'Read the *following* words and then forget them,' Grey Crow said.

decide:1.en: The signal split at the crossroads — one lead went east toward the harbour, one went west into the factory district. Grey Crow was gone. Ali looked at me and said nothing. I had thirty seconds to *decide*. The rain erased every sound except my own breathing and the low hum of the city grid above.
decide:1.cnHint: 信号在路口一分为二，灰鸦不见了，我必须自己____走哪条路。
decide:1.hook: I chose a direction and ran before I could change my mind.
decide:1.line: 'You have to *decide* now — the signal won't wait,' Ali said.

passage:2.en: The maintenance tunnel beneath Platform Nine was narrow and wet. Grey Crow led me through the *passage* at a crouch, our boots loud against the metal floor. Halfway through, I spotted something scratched into the wall: a signal map, fresh enough to still show copper under the rust.
passage:2.cnHint: 在站台下方的狭窄____里，我发现了墙上刻出的信号地图。
passage:2.hook: The map pointed somewhere no rookie should ever go.
passage:2.line: 'This *passage* leads to Zero's last known drop point,' Grey Crow whispered.

base:2.en: The chip was cracked, but its *base* was intact — a flat black square no wider than my thumbnail. Ali placed it under the scanner light and tilted her head. 'Someone filed the serial number off,' she said. Rain hammered the window. Outside, a drone circled the block for the third time.
base:2.cnHint: 那枚芯片的____完好无损，阿里发现序列号被人故意磨掉了。
base:2.hook: That drone outside was not city patrol.
base:2.line: 'The *base* still holds the original encryption key,' Ali said quietly.

section:2.en: Grey Crow handed me a torn printout. One *section* of the city grid was blacked out — manually, with ink, not a system error. That block covered the old harbor warehouse district. No cameras. No registered residents. I had passed it a hundred times and never thought twice.
section:2.cnHint: 城市地图上有一个____被人用墨水手动涂黑，那片区域毫无监控记录。
section:2.hook: Someone had hidden that district before I was even born.
section:2.line: 'That *section* has been off the official map for twenty years,' Grey Crow said.

answer:2.en: I knocked twice, then once, the code Ali gave me. Nothing. I knocked again. The door stayed shut. I pressed my ear to the cold steel and heard a faint hum — a data stream, live and close. The *answer* was not words. It was a sequence of tones, rising and falling like breath.
answer:2.cnHint: 门后没有人语回应，传来的____却是一串奇怪的音调序列。
answer:2.hook: That tone sequence matched the broadcast from last night.
answer:2.line: 'That sound is the only *answer* Zero ever gives,' Ali warned.

study:2.en: The room looked like a *study* — shelves of binders, a lamp still warm, a half-empty cup of coffee on the desk. But every binder was blank inside. Ali ran her finger along the shelf edge and stopped. Hidden behind the last binder was a slim drive, still blinking green.
study:2.cnHint: 这间看起来像____的房间里，每本档案夹都是空的，却藏着一个仍在运行的数据盘。
study:2.hook: The drive was transmitting — right now, to somewhere unknown.
study:2.line: 'This *study* was staged for anyone who came looking,' Grey Crow said flatly.

mark:2.en: I almost missed it. On the underside of the park bench, pressed into the wet paint, was a small circle with a line through it — Zero's *mark*. Ali photographed it without touching it. Grey Crow stood watch, collar up against the rain, eyes on the far end of the street.
mark:2.cnHint: 公园长椅底部藏着零点的____，阿里悄悄拍下了它。
mark:2.hook: Zero had been here within the last hour.
mark:2.line: 'That *mark* means the package already moved,' Ali said, voice tight.

choice:2.en: Grey Crow laid two drives on the table. One held the encrypted broadcast source. The other held the names of every operative in the city. 'You only get one,' he said. 'Take your time.' I had ten seconds before the timer on the table hit zero. It was not much of a *choice*.
choice:2.cnHint: 面对两个数据盘，我只能拿走一个，这个____几乎让人窒息。
choice:2.hook: The timer hit three seconds before my hand moved.
choice:2.line: 'There is no safe *choice* here — only a less dangerous one,' Grey Crow said.

part:2.en: The signal came in fragments. I could only decode one *part* of the message before the channel went dark: a street name, a number, and the word 'tonight.' Ali wrote it on her palm in marker. Grey Crow was already pulling on his coat. The rain outside shifted from drizzle to downpour.
part:2.cnHint: 信号只传来了消息的一个____——一个街道名和"今晚"这个词。
part:2.hook: One missing part could mean the difference between a trap and a rescue.
part:2.line: 'That *part* of the message is the only piece Zero wanted us to find,' Grey Crow said.

letter:2.en: The rain hammered the roof of sub-station nine. I found the package wedged behind a loose wall panel — no sender, no stamp. Inside sat a single folded note. Each *letter* of the first line was printed in a different ink, as if many hands had built it together. Someone had worked hard to hide who wrote this.
letter:2.cnHint: 我在墙板后发现一个包裹，里面的纸条上每个____都用不同颜色的墨水印成。
letter:2.hook: The last character was still wet.
letter:2.line: Grey Crow said, 'Every *letter* here is a key — read them in order.'

sheet:2.en: Ali spread it flat on the table under the cold light. It was one *sheet* of thin paper, nearly transparent, covered edge to edge in tiny printed symbols. No word I could read. No gap I could find. The whole surface buzzed with hidden meaning, like a city map drawn by someone who did not want you to arrive.
sheet:2.cnHint: 阿栗把那____薄纸铺在桌上，上面密密麻麻全是无法辨读的符号。
sheet:2.hook: Then the light flickered, and the symbols shifted.
sheet:2.line: 'This *sheet* was torn from a broadcast log,' Ali said quietly.

corresponding:2.en: Zero had left nine symbols on the wall. Grey Crow handed me a small card with nine shapes and their *corresponding* sounds written below each one. Match shape to sound, sound to meaning. Simple in theory. But two shapes were identical, and their sounds were opposites. Someone had built a trap right into the code.
corresponding:2.cnHint: 零点在墙上留下九个符号，灰鸦给了我一张卡片，上面列出每个符号____的读音。
corresponding:2.hook: I matched the last pair — and the wall hummed.
corresponding:2.line: 'Find the *corresponding* signal and you find the source,' Grey Crow told me.

choose:2.en: Grey Crow pointed to two doors at the end of the corridor. One led toward the old broadcast tower. One led down to the flooded lower level. I had sixty seconds before the grid reset and both doors locked. I had to *choose* with nothing but a faint sound and a cold feeling in my chest guiding me.
choose:2.cnHint: 走廊尽头有两扇门，我必须在六十秒内____其中一扇，否则两扇都会锁死。
choose:2.hook: I stepped forward — and the lights died.
choose:2.line: 'You must *choose* now,' Grey Crow said, 'there is no third path.'

single:2.en: I scanned the entire broadcast log. Forty pages of noise, static, broken signals. Then I found it — a *single* clean line of text, sitting alone in the middle of page thirty-one, surrounded by garbage data. It did not belong there. It was too clear, too neat. Someone had planted it and waited for someone like me to notice.
single:2.cnHint: 整份广播记录里，只有____一行文字清晰完整，夹在满页乱码的第三十一页正中央。
single:2.hook: The line read: 'You are already late.'
single:2.line: 'That *single* word changes everything we thought we knew,' Ali said.

line:2.en: The coded map showed a grid of streets. Most were marked in grey. But one *line* ran from the harbour wall straight to the old signal house, drawn in red, thinner than the rest, easy to miss. Ali said it was a maintenance path, closed for years. Grey Crow said nothing. He just tapped it twice and looked at me.
line:2.cnHint: 地图上大多数街道都是灰色的，只有一条____从港口直通旧信号屋，用红色细线标出。
line:2.hook: Footsteps echoed — someone else had found the map first.
line:2.line: 'Follow that *line* and do not stop for anything,' Grey Crow said.

become:2.en: Six months ago this district was full of open signals and loud voices. Now every channel was dark. Ali told me that silence had *become* the loudest warning in Harbor City — when everyone goes quiet at once, something bad is very close. I checked my receiver. Every frequency empty. Every band dead. The whole city was holding its breath.
become:2.cnHint: 阿栗告诉我，在Harbor City，沉默已经____最响亮的警告——所有频道同时消失意味着危险将至。
become:2.hook: Then one frequency crackled back to life — just one.
become:2.line: Ali whispered, 'Silence has *become* their favourite weapon.'

centre:2.en: The signal was strongest at the old transit hall — a wide dark space in the *centre* of the eastern block, abandoned since the flood of 2081. I moved through the broken doors, rain still dripping from my coat. The hall was empty. But a single chair sat in the exact middle of the floor, facing the main entrance, as if someone had just left.
centre:2.cnHint: 信号在东区废弃的旧中转大厅____最强，我进入后发现厅内空无一人，却有一把椅子正对着入口。
centre:2.hook: On the chair was an envelope with my name on it.
centre:2.line: 'The *centre* of the grid is where they always leave the message,' Grey Crow said.

bank:2.en: The rain hit the *bank* terminal hard, its screen flickering in the dark. I pressed my palm against the glass. Inside, rows of locked data vaults held encrypted files from Zero's last known operation. Grey Crow had told me: 'All roads lead here.' I was about to find out why.
bank:2.cnHint: 我在河边的数据____终端前，发现了零点上次行动留下的加密档案。
bank:2.hook: The vault door clicked open — but I never touched it.
bank:2.line: 'Every *bank* of stolen data leads back to the same name,' Grey Crow said quietly.

statement:2.en: A single *statement* was scratched into the wall of the abandoned relay station: 'ZERO WAS HERE BEFORE THE FLOOD.' Ali shone her light across it. The letters were fresh. The dust on the floor was not. Someone had been back — recently — and they wanted us to know.
statement:2.cnHint: 废弃中继站的墙上刻着一句____，暗示零点曾在洪水前到访此地。
statement:2.hook: The ink was still wet; the room smelled of rain and lies.
statement:2.line: 'That *statement* was left for you,' Ali said, stepping back.

identify:2.en: Grey Crow handed me a blurred photo pulled from a broken signal feed. 'Can you *identify* the symbol in the corner?' I leaned close. It matched the coded mark I had seen on every sealed door in the flooded district. My hand went cold. This was not a random sign.
identify:2.cnHint: 灰鸦让我从模糊的信号图像中____出某个暗号标记。
identify:2.hook: The symbol pulsed once on my scanner — then vanished.
identify:2.line: '*Identify* the mark fast,' Grey Crow said. 'We have ninety seconds.'

comprehension:2.en: The broadcast lasted four seconds. Most people would hear only static. My *comprehension* of layered signal code told me otherwise: beneath the noise was a street name, a time, and a warning. Ali grabbed my arm. She had heard it too. Neither of us moved for a long moment.
comprehension:2.cnHint: 普通人只听到杂音，但我凭借对信号代码的____，从广播中提取出了关键信息。
comprehension:2.hook: The warning said: 'Do not come alone — or at all.'
comprehension:2.line: 'Your *comprehension* of this code is the only thing keeping us alive,' Ali whispered.

require:2.en: The locked archive door had a keypad and a small speaker. A flat voice said, 'Access will *require* voice confirmation from an authorized agent.' I looked at Ali. She looked at me. We had no authorization. What we did have was a recording of Grey Crow's voice, three seconds long.
require:2.cnHint: 档案室的门____语音授权才能打开，而我们手里只有灰鸦三秒钟的录音。
require:2.hook: The speaker crackled — then asked for a second phrase.
require:2.line: 'They *require* more than a name,' Ali said. 'They want a code word.'

least:2.en: I had three routes into the signal tower. The longest was the safest. The shortest was exposed and lit. The middle path was dark and unmapped. I chose the last one — not because it was easy, but because Zero would *least* expect anyone to come from a direction with no exit.
least:2.cnHint: 我选择了零点____可能预料到的那条路线进入信号塔。
least:2.hook: Halfway in, I heard footsteps — coming from exactly that direction.
least:2.line: 'At *least* tell me you have a way out,' Ali said through the earpiece.

following:2.en: I found the note tucked inside a cracked junction box. It read: 'Do the *following* — go to level three, find the red cable, pull it twice.' Simple enough. Too simple. Grey Crow had taught me that clear instructions in this city always hid a harder test inside them.
following:2.cnHint: 我在接线盒里发现一张字条，要求我按照____的步骤行事，但灰鸦教过我别轻信简单指令。
following:2.hook: I pulled the cable twice — and the lights went out city-wide.
following:2.line: 'The *following* message was meant only for you,' Grey Crow said without looking up.

decide:2.en: Ali and I stood at the split corridor under the old bridge. Left led to Zero's last signal point. Right led to the exit and safety. Grey Crow was not answering. We had to *decide* in seconds. The rain hammered the concrete above us. I looked at the left turn and exhaled.
decide:2.cnHint: 阿栗和我在地下走廊岔路口必须快速____：是追踪零点还是撤退。
decide:2.hook: I stepped left — and heard Zero's voice echo from the right.
decide:2.line: 'You have to *decide* now,' Ali said. 'He already knows we are here.'
